children: The U.K. is narrowing its deficit, but that isn't enough to reverse its rising debt, Moody's Ratings says. The rating agency expects the U.K. will narrow its deficit, which reached 5.3% of GDP in 2025, to 4.5% in 2026 and 4% in 2027. The U.K.'s budget for 2027 also confirms its government's commitment to reducing the country's deficit, Moody's says. However, Moody's still expects government debt will grow to 106% of GDP by the end of the decade. Interest rates are expected to stay high relative to revenue. The long average maturity of government debt and deep domestic capital markets limit refinancing and liquidity risks, as well, Moody's says. (katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)
